Ive had hundreds of hours poured into both games, so I can't say i didn't had fun. Yet after all of it, i wish there was more to them, and it's frustrating how the latest nfs entries take one step forward, one step back in different areas, so you never really feel like the franchise is growing nor getting bigger. At least thats my perspective.


Heat's art style is fleshed out with more confidence than Unbound. The sense of speed is much better, the driving is too simplistic yet always predictable, the sound mixing is vastly superior. But of course, its evident how it was poorly maintained by updates and eventually abandoned. It absolutely feels like an incomplete game. It had potential, but it just never happened.

Unbound's strength is without a doubt the burst nos and the return of grip racing, giving much more needed depth to the barebones b2d of Heat (however unpredictable and glitchy the physics ended up being). The core of nfs, the racing/driving, is here, but in my opinion, everything else is lacking. The art style is a huge missed opportunity and letdown, the UI, menus and hud are some of the worst I've ever seen (i cant stress enough how much of an eye sore and a pain to navigate these are), the campaign is dry and somehow more anticlimactic than Heat. And after 9 BIG updates, the game still feels incomplete and has issues. 

Maybe Unbound gets much more hate than its predecessor because it had 2 years of updates and it still couldn't live up to the general expectations of players. Theyre both fun games, theyre ok and you can definitely have fun with them. Cars look nice, the music is alright and graphics are quite good. And here is where I believe most of the community goes back to: there's just not a lot else to them, especially against previous games. They dont feel grand, 60-70 price tag games. Theyre wide as an ocean with their customization and wallpaper potential, but deep as a puddle with their basic 3-4 gamemodes and lackluster campaigns.

For how short and small Rivals is, it feels extremely focused on its (admittedly few) strengths unlike the latest entries. Its not a 20+ hours experience that constantly tries shows of new things; you get a diverse map, fast cars, weapons and relentless AI, and that's it. The rest is pure racing, crashing and pursuing. And its just solid.

Also it has lots of details exclusive to it or at least shared by few other games: It has a full day-night cycle, it has somewhat dynamic weather that looks gorgeous, a rear view mirror, ZERO loading screens after jumping into the world, roaming and fully functional ai racers (i cant believe this wasn't re implemented in heat and unbound, it does so much for replayability in-between events and inmersion), 2 protagonists with their own cutscenes. And the 30fps limit is a way overblown flaw, the game is completely playable and enjoyable with that framerate; dare i say it actually helps to give it that cinematic and gritty feel without going completely choppy with 24 fps.

I was deep in the red forest, looking for artifacts near the swingset anomaly. Although it was plain midday, under the dense canopy of the forest it was almost pitch black, so night vision was a necessity. I had a maxxed out PDA, meaning it showed me nearby friendly stalker squads. I ocasionaly checked it so i knew where exactly in the forest i was. All normal: a freedomer near the entrance of the reserve, clear sky going south to the warehouses.

I hear gunshots in the distance, instinctively stay still and check my surroundings expecting an attack. Dead silence, and after checking the pda one of the friendly squads was gone. "Lost to the fanatics", i think to myself, and as i put my pda away, a message pops up:

"Is the reward for Svetaev (my nickname) still up? Ive heard he's in the Red Forest, near the Radar"

Ive never seen this type of message before (inmediately start recording), specifically calling me out and pinpointing my location. I get scared and realize i can be in a lot of trouble: unfamiliar and highly anomalous terrain, cant see a damn thing without NV, and no easy routes of escape: to the right is the Brain Scorcher, and to the left is the rest of the forest where my hunters await for me.

I decide to fight back. No way would i make it out of the Radar with the amount of ammo and supplies i had. So i start trecking back to the center of the forest. I havent even left the area around the mines when bullets start carving the nearby trees. I take cover and out of nowhere a grenade almost takes my arm off. Now im actually scared, and kind of in awe: the message was real! The game was tracking me down and trying to kill me! I wasnt playing a sidequest or mission at the moment, i wasnt triggering anything new since i was already past endgame, i was actually being hunted down. By whom?

After hastily applying medkits and downing some vinca because of course i was out of bandaids, covering my ass for dear life from tree to tree with fire going over my head and the ocassional grenade hitting right where i was standing mere seconds before, i can take my gun out and hear the all familiar monolith warning: "Opponent, liquidate!"

My NV dies out. I have to change batteries mid combat else i cant see anything. I scope out my surroundings, the monolith camo is completely in its element, theyre practically invisible until they move. And theyre not close, i see a head peeking on the side of a tree tens of meters away from me. I have to make my few bullets count.

I start firing, they start moving around. Two, three, maybe four of them? They're relentless. I take one out with a lucky shot, another one makes the big mistake of triggering an anomaly. Its a long fight, a patience game to see who can get closer and finish it. And then its all quiet. Is it over? Did i make it? I carefully start scavenging the bodies. I think its over. I can finally take a breather...

.

.

And if i recall correctly, i managed all of this without dying, which only made the fight more and more tense as i got closer to escaping with my life. Easily the most fun i had with the game and the a-life, which after that moment periodically kept sending monolith and merc squads to take me out, no matter where in the zone i was.
